body.statement: The randomized interval problem for \(\mathcal E_3\) is exactly the finite linear program specified by the three-block LP construction. At \(\alpha=0.1\) and \(\gamma=0\), with all available potential outcomes in \(\{-M,0,M\}\), its minimax expected length is exactly \(\mathfrak L^{(3)}_{0.1,0}=0.7M\). The hull-plus-singletons policy and analytic dual in the zero-drift certificate are respectively primal and dual feasible with common value \(0.7M\). On the control-assignment record each of the three observationally indistinguishable target values has marginal conditional coverage \(0.8\), but auxiliary randomization need not cover the two extreme targets jointly; therefore those marginal constraints do not imply conditional expected length \(1.6M\). No exact value is asserted here for positive drift budgets or for the concurrent-only restriction without a displayed matching primal--dual certificate.
body.justification: The fully determined smallest decision problem validates the action randomization logic and supplies a reproducible exact check on the all-interval formulation.
body.gap: The NCC literature uses simulation for small platform designs; it does not solve this specified uniformly honest randomized variable-length interval problem exactly.
body.consumer: The finite LP, explicit policy, and analytic dual become a regression test for implementations of the randomized-interval decision problem.
